items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Charlie Glenn gave me $10 and a bottle of liquor.

ctx.x: talking to you? August third. And we opened up -- at Joe's Joe Ziggy Johnson got the chorus girls, Marl doing the writing, (unintelligible), we got a guy in St. Louis writing, and I'll tell you what good readers we were -- we could spell a little bit, but this was a big time show; we ain't never hit nothing this big time before in our life! And nobody could play. I ain't never directed a band in my life. My right hand to God.

But Charlie Glenn sat on the railing on the side; he said, "Now time is passing," and he said, "Somebody has to open the show tonight. And Maur is pulling his hair out. And I'm listening, and I'm watching everything he was saying, so when it got so critical, I came out, I said, "Well, just give me an opportunity to do something. Let me help", because I'm carrying my wife with me; I got my automobile out, away from home, got rent to pay back here -- still holding the house, and here I am, they gonna put us out…
I got up there and I directed that band and was wobbly kneed, but desperate.
